original_value: In this article, an adaptive control logic is proposed to serve as a supervisory control system sufficient to curb the adverse effects due to modelling uncertainties and external disturbances. The control logic belongs to the class of adaptive control methodologies. The attractive attribute of this technique is that only the superior features of each individual candidate controller are obtained by applying appropriate weight to these controllers. In order to prove its effectiveness and applicability, the benchmark problem for stabilization of cart-inverted pendulum system is carried out using this technique. The system performance is tried against that with each individual candidate controllers existing techniques. In addition, the simulation-based analysis is strengthened by analysing the performance of a real-time cart-inverted pendulum system setup, stabilized using the proposed control logic.

result.paraphrase: This article proposes an adaptive control logic as a supervisory control system capable of mitigating the harmful effects of modelling uncertainties and external disturbances. Falling within adaptive control methodologies, the technique’s main advantage is that appropriate weighting of the candidate controllers extracts only their best features. To demonstrate effectiveness and applicability, it is tested on the benchmark cart-inverted pendulum stabilization problem and its performance is compared with that of each individual candidate controller in existing techniques. The simulation results are further supported by analysis of a real-time cart-inverted pendulum setup stabilized with the proposed control logic.
